title: Thanksgiving Storm Chaos: Millions Face Outages, Flooding, and Travel Delays After Historic Holiday Coast-to-Coast Batter
snippet: Severe Thanksgiving storms slammed the East Coast and Midwest with torrential rain, heavy snow, and fierce winds, knocking out power for hundreds of thousands and forcing the historic postponement of the Macy's parade.
content:
A punishing Thanksgiving storm system wreaked havoc across the Northeast and Midwest over the holiday weekend, causing widespread power outages, severe travel disruptions, and unprecedented flooding that pushed coastal communities into emergency response mode.

By Friday afternoon, over 440,000 utility customers remained without electricity across the Northeast and Midwest, down from a storm peak of more than 800,000 households on Thursday night, according to tracking data from PowerOutage.us. Pennsylvania took the brunt of the blackouts with more than 109,000 customers in the dark, while New Jersey reported 68,000 outages and Maryland logged over 54,000.

Travel Nightmare Hits Holiday Commuters

The severe weather threw nationwide holiday travel into turmoil. Flight-tracking service FlightAware reported over 2,200 U.S. flight delays and more than 100 cancellations by Friday afternoon, following Thursday's brutal tally of 2,500 delays and 460 cancellations.

On the ground, major transportation corridors were severed by rising waters and high winds. The nearly 18-mile Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel in Virginia was temporarily shut down Thursday morning due to dangerously high wind gusts. In North Carolina, coastal highway NC 12 was shut after seawater breached oceanfront dunes, stranding access to Hatteras Island. Localized rain gauge readings reached astounding levels in coastal North Carolina, where Emerald Isle recorded over 9.1 inches of rain.

New York City's Historic Parade Delays

In New York City, relentless precipitation delivered up to 3 inches of rain alongside ferocious wind gusts reaching 56 mph at LaGuardia Airport. The wind conditions posed severe safety hazards around Manhattan's high-rises, forcing organizers to postpone the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday—a rare move in the parade's long history.

The shift forced visitors to quickly pivot. A 500-member high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, had to launch a rapid community fundraising effort, successfully raising $350,000 in short order to extend their stay in Manhattan for two additional nights so they could still march.

Emergency crews across Gotham performed multiple water rescues from flooded vehicles. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned residents against navigating submerged streets. "There is no destination worth your safety," Mamdani emphasized during a briefing.

States of Emergency and Coastal Flooding

Dynamic tidal surges inundated communities from North Carolina up through New England. Governors Mikie Sherrill of New Jersey and Kathy Hochul of New York both declared states of emergency as water covered roads and swamped neighborhoods.

In Southern New Jersey, historic high tides swamped coastal towns including Avalon, Ocean City, and Margate City. U.S. Route 30 into Atlantic City was forced to close in both directions. Meanwhile, near Philadelphia, Chester County Hospital endured a temporary power disruption, and residents in Springfield Township briefly evacuated after a fallen tree threatened a local propane tank.

Further west, the storm produced heavy snowfall across the Midwest. St. Louis recorded 7.3 inches of snow, while parts of eastern Missouri saw up to 15 inches. In Wentzville, Missouri, heavy snow accumulation caused the roof of an empty local ice arena to collapse early Thursday morning.

Forecasters warn that the Northeast isn't entirely in the clear yet, with another wave of rainy weather taking aim at Boston, Philadelphia, and New York early next week.
